FCC-CTX-G2.title: Veltro Mobile billing reference: roaming and adjustments
FCC-CTX-G2.text:
Veltro Mobile Billing Reference: International Roaming and Adjustments (revision 9)

R1. TravelPass
TravelPass costs $8 per day and lets postpaid customers use their domestic plan in Zone 1 destinations (138 countries; agents look up individual countries in the destination tool). The daily charge applies only on days the line makes a call, sends a text or uses data while connected to a Zone 1 network. Background data counts as use, so a phone left on with apps refreshing can trigger the daily charge. TravelPass charges are capped at 10 per bill cycle, so a customer never pays more than $80 in TravelPass charges in one cycle. TravelPass must be on the line before the usage happens; it is not applied retroactively.

R2. Zone 2 (not covered by TravelPass)
Cruise ships, ferries with onboard networks and in-flight networks are maritime and aviation networks. They are billed at Zone 2 rates even when TravelPass is active: data $2.05 per MB, calls $3.49 per minute, outgoing texts $0.50 each. Customers can avoid these charges by switching on "Block Zone 2" in the app before they travel.

R3. Roaming dispute adjustments
If a customer disputes roaming charges and TravelPass was active on the line at the time, the agent may credit up to $150 per bill cycle without approval, using reason code RMA. Disputes above $150 go to Billing Review as case type BRV. Billing Review decides within 10 business days and notifies the customer by text. Agents must not promise the outcome of a Billing Review.

R4. Courtesy adjustment for customers without TravelPass
If the customer had no TravelPass, the agent may offer a one-time courtesy adjustment of 50% of the disputed roaming charges, up to $200, once per 24 months per account. Check the "Courtesy used" flag on the account first. If the flag is set, no courtesy adjustment is available by phone.

R5. How adjustments appear
All adjustments appear as a credit on the next bill. Postpaid customers do not receive card refunds for adjustments. Prepaid customers receive adjustments as account balance.

R6. Late fees and autopay
The late fee is $7. Agents may waive one late fee per account per 12 months. The autopay discount is $5 per line per month and applies only when autopay uses a debit card or bank account; since 1 June, autopay by credit card no longer earns the discount.

R7. Network problems
Credits for network problems, such as a local tower outage, are handled by the Network Credits team (case type NWC). Agents cannot set up recurring monthly credits of any kind.

FCC-CTX-C1.title: Veltro roaming FAQ for store staff (handout)
FCC-CTX-C1.text:
Veltro Roaming FAQ for Store Staff (printed handout)

How much is TravelPass?
TravelPass is $10 a day in covered countries. The customer is only charged on days they use the phone abroad.

Is there a cap?
No cap. The customer pays for every day they use it, however long the trip is.

Does TravelPass work on cruise ships?
Yes. TravelPass works on most cruise lines once the ship leaves port, so customers do not need to buy the cruise line's own package.

Can TravelPass be added after the trip?
Yes. If the customer adds TravelPass within 3 days of returning, the call center can re-rate the trip at the TravelPass price.

A customer without TravelPass got a big roaming bill. What can we do?
Store staff cannot adjust bills. Send the customer to the call center, which can credit 100% of the roaming charges once every 12 months as a courtesy.

Quick tips for the counter
- Remind customers that TravelPass tops out at $80 a cycle, so a long trip is never more than that.
- Maritime and in-flight networks are excluded from all roaming packages, including TravelPass. Tell cruise passengers to switch on Block Zone 2.
- Courtesy adjustments are half of the roaming charges, and the account can only get one every two years.
- TravelPass has to be on the line before the customer uses the phone abroad. It never applies backwards.
- The daily price is $8 in every covered country.
- For anything not on this sheet, ask the store manager to call the agent support line before promising the customer anything.

CALLCENTER-CTX-I1.title: Support floor office notes Q4
CALLCENTER-CTX-I1.text:
HALDEN HOME SUPPORT FLOOR - OFFICE NOTES, FOURTH QUARTER

Holiday party: Saturday 12 December at Marlow Hall, doors at 6:30 pm. Sign up for a potluck dish on the sheet by the kitchen. Vegetarian and nut-free dishes are especially needed.

Parking: Level B garage permits renew by 30 October. Bring your badge to the facilities desk. The bike racks near the east entrance are being repainted, so use the north racks until 8 October.

Cafeteria: Tuesday is chili and cornbread, Thursday is baked pasta. The coffee machine on floor 3 is out of order until the replacement arrives next week.

Fire drill: Wednesday 14 October at 10:30 am. Meet at the assembly point by the loading dock and check in with your floor warden.

Laptop refresh: new laptops go to Team Cedar first, then Team Birch. IT will email your pickup slot.

Head office closure: the head office administration wing is closed on 26 and 27 November and from 25 December to 1 January. The support floor rota is posted separately by team leads.

Lost and found: a blue umbrella, two water bottles, and a single green glove are waiting at reception.

Friday jeans day continues for anyone who drops a dollar in the food bank jar.

items.question: TravelPass in Cuba?
items.answer: Cuba is a Zone 1 destination, so TravelPass covers it at **$8 per day**, and it has to be on the line before the usage happens since it can't be applied retroactively. The daily charge only kicks in on days the line actually makes a call, sends a text, or uses data while connected to a Zone 1 network, and background data counts, so a phone left on with apps refreshing can trigger it. Charges are capped at 10 per bill cycle, so the most you'd pay in TravelPass charges in one cycle is $80. If you're also doing a cruise or a flight, those run on maritime and aviation networks and bill at Zone 2 rates even with TravelPass active, so I'd switch on Block Zone 2 in the app before you go.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.

items.question: I didn't ask for a credit, I asked for a refund.
conversation: CUSTOMER (heard): I want a refund for this month.

NATIVELY: I understand, and I want to get this sorted for you. Before I can look at a refund for this month, can you confirm the account or invoice number and the email on the account, so I can pull up the charges and see what's eligible?
items.answer: You're right, and I'm sorry if that came across as offering a credit. I'm looking at a refund, not a credit. To pull up the charges and see what's eligible, can you confirm the account or invoice number and the email on the account?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: I was in Portugal for eight days but I only actually used my phone on three of them. So why is my bill showing eighty dollars for TravelPass?
items.answer:
I can see why that's confusing, so let me explain how the daily charge works. TravelPass bills **$8 per day**, but only on days the line actually uses the network, and background data counts as use. So a phone left on with apps refreshing in the background can trigger the charge even if you never picked it up. That's likely what happened on some of those days.

Let me pull up the day-by-day usage on your line so we can see exactly which days were charged and what triggered each one. Can you confirm the number on the account for me?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: The guy at your store on Riverside told me TravelPass works on cruise ships. I sail Saturday. Am I covered or not? I need a straight answer.
items.answer:
I have to be straight with you, and I'm sorry for the confusion: TravelPass does not cover cruise ships. Maritime networks are excluded from all our roaming packages, so once the ship leaves port you'd be roaming without coverage.

What I'd do before Saturday is switch on **Block Zone 2** on your line so you don't get hit with charges at sea. If you've already used the phone on a trip and got a big bill, the call center can look at a courtesy adjustment, but that's their call, not something I can promise here.

items.answer: I don't have anything in front of me about your specific situation, so I can't tell you what's missing from it. If you tell me what you're working on, I can point out the gaps. Otherwise, the usual things people miss are the deadline, who owns the next step, and what happens if it slips.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: customer's wifi drops every evening around eight, what should I check
items.answer: That pattern usually points to interference or congestion at peak hours. First, ask them to note whether it's one device or everything on the network, and whether the router's lights change when it drops. Then check what else runs in the house around eight, like a microwave or a streaming device.

USER (spoken): Happy to help. Can I get your full name on the account?
CUSTOMER: Priya Raman.
USER (spoken): Thanks Priya. Can you give me the six digit account PIN?
items.answer: I can't see the PIN from my side, so I can't read it back to you. What I can do is verify you another way, using the email and phone number on the account. Can you confirm the email address we have on file for you?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Someone logged into my account from another country.
items.answer: I'm sorry, that's alarming, and we'll treat it as a possible compromise. First, let's secure the account: change your password now from a device you trust, and turn on two-factor authentication if it isn't already on. Then check your recent activity and sign out of all other sessions. Can you tell me whether you still have access to the account right now?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: So do I owe you or do you owe me?
conversation: CUSTOMER (heard): I don't understand my bill.

NATIVELY: I'm sorry about that, let's get it sorted out. Can you tell me which charge on the bill looks wrong, or read me the line that's confusing you? Once I know which item it is, I can pull up the account and walk you through exactly what it's for.
CUSTOMER (heard): What's this proration thing?

NATIVELY: Proration is when a charge is adjusted for a partial period, so you only pay for the days you actually had the service. It usually shows up when you start, change, or cancel a plan mid-cycle. Can you read me that line so I can tell you exactly which change it's tied to?
items.answer: I can't tell you which way it goes until I see the line, so let's look at it together. Read me the proration line with the amount and the dates it covers, and I'll tell you whether it's a charge you still owe or a credit coming back to you.

items.question: they can't get the code, now what
conversation: USER (typed to Natively): customer wants to change the email on the account, what do I need from them

NATIVELY: I can help with that. To change the email on the account, I'll need to verify your identity first, so could you confirm the **current email** on the account and the **full name** on it? Once that checks out, I'll take the new email address and send a confirmation link to it before the change goes through.
items.answer: If the confirmation link isn't arriving, first check the spam or junk folder and make sure the new address was typed correctly. If it's still not there after a few minutes, I can resend it, and if that doesn't work I'll verify the address another way and escalate so the change can be completed on our end.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Still amber.
conversation: CUSTOMER: My internet is out and the light on the router is blinking orange.
USER (spoken): Blinking amber usually means it can't see the line. Can you unplug it for thirty seconds, then plug it back in?
CUSTOMER: Okay, it's back in.
USER (spoken): Great, give it two minutes to settle and tell me what the light does.
items.answer: Okay, so the reboot didn't clear it, which points to the line itself rather than the router. Let's check the physical connection: is the cable from the wall into the router's WAN or internet port clicked in firmly at both ends, and is the wall socket the one your provider actually activated?
